title: Irrationality of ∛3
description: Proves that the cube root of 3 is irrational using Mathlib's irrational_nrt_of_notint_nrt. Establishes that 3 is not a perfect cube (1³ = 1 < 3 < 8 = 2³), hence cbrt3 = 3^(1/3) is not an integer, hence irrational. Mirrors the proof structure of CubeRoot2Irrational. 5 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. Fully machine-verified using Mathlib's Irrational and irrational_nrt_of_notint_nrt.
originalContributions: three_not_perfect_cube: ¬∃ n : ℤ, n³ = 3, proved by integer bounds 1³ < 3 < 2³

overview.historicalContext: The irrationality of ∛3 follows the same proof pattern as ∛2. Both are instances of the general theorem that n√m is irrational when m is not a perfect n-th power. These results are classical in elementary number theory and appear as exercises in introductory courses.
overview.text: Identical structure to CubeRoot2Irrational: (1) cbrt3_cubed via rpow composition, (2) three_not_perfect_cube by integer bound analysis (n ≤ 0 gives n³ ≤ 0 < 3; n ≥ 2 gives n³ ≥ 8 > 3; n = 1 gives 1 ≠ 3), (3) cbrt3_not_int derived from three_not_perfect_cube, (4) irrational_cbrt3 via irrational_nrt_of_notint_nrt 3 3.
overview.proofStrategy: Same as CubeRoot2Irrational but with the value 3 instead of 2. The bounds 0 < n < 2 force n = 1, and 1³ = 1 ≠ 3 by norm_num.
keyInsights: The proof structure is identical to ∛2: only the constant changes
3 lies strictly between 1³ = 1 and 2³ = 8, so it is not a perfect cube
irrational_nrt_of_notint_nrt is a powerful general lemma for this class of results

conclusion.summary: ∛3 is irrational, proved by showing 3 is not a perfect cube. Mirror of CubeRoot2Irrational. 5 theorems, 0 axioms, 83 lines.
conclusion.implications: Together with CubeRoot2Irrational, demonstrates the template for proving irrationality of cube roots via Mathlib's irrational_nrt_of_notint_nrt. The pattern extends to all m that are not perfect cubes.
openQuestions: Prove the general theorem: ∛m is irrational iff m is not a perfect cube
